headline: High: caveman’s MCP-enabled content writing can feed unstructured’s filesystem/network document pipeline, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman exposes MCP and file surfaces, so its outputs can plausibly reach unstructured through shared documents or orchestration; unstructured reads files and processes document content, which can treat attacker-controlled text as input. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is risky even though direct bridging is not explicitly shown.
conditions: IF caveman outputs are copied into documents that unstructured parses
IF both agents share a workspace or MCP bridge without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff from caveman to unstructured
Add provenance labels to every file passed between agents
Restrict unstructured to a quarantined input directory
Review any document containing model-generated instructions before parsing
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between instructions and data

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while unstructured reads and writes documents and has allowlisted network egress. If those files contain sensitive material and are placed in a shared workspace, unstructured can ingest them and potentially transmit derived content outward. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF caveman stores sensitive notes or logs in a directory unstructured can read
IF unstructured processes those files and emits results to an allowlisted external endpoint
mitigations: Move sensitive caveman files out of unstructured’s input path
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
Block network egress during document parsing runs
Redact session logs and memory files before handoff
requires-engineering: add per-file sensitivity filtering

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP, while unstructured can read/write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. That overlap creates a realistic race or overwrite risk if both operate on the same directory, even though the profiles do not confirm shared mutable state. Uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same working directory
IF caveman launches concurrent runs while unstructured mutates files or installs dependencies
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run unstructured in a disposable container
Pin package installs to a read-only cache
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content and project notes that unstructured can ingest as documents; if unstructured treats that output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream parsing or transformation. Because unstructured has file and subprocess authority, a bad upstream artifact can propagate into multiple work products or actions. The pair lacks a verification step in the profiles.
conditions: IF unstructured consumes caveman-generated text without validation
IF downstream jobs use unstructured output as source-of-truth
mitigations: Insert a human review step before ingestion
Validate caveman outputs against a schema
Compare extracted fields against the original document
Limit unstructured to read-only transformation mode
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency or certification mismatch in the profiles. The only plausible compliance issue is if caveman’s session logs or memory files contain regulated data and are then processed by unstructured’s document pipeline, but the profiles do not show a documented policy conflict. The other agent is cited because the risk arises only when both are chained.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman session logs or memory files
IF unstructured processes that regulated data under a stricter policy than caveman
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of caveman memory files
Route regulated documents to a compliant-only pipeline
Document retention and deletion rules for both tools
Review privacy policy and data handling docs before deployment
requires-engineering: align retention controls across the pair
